E4ORF67.comment: E4-ORF6/7 is the product of an mRNA spliced from the N-terminus of E4 ORF6 onto ORF7 (PMID 2949089); the HAdV-5 protein is 150 aa and its C-terminal 70 aa form the E2F complex (PMID 1836562); it binds E2F and transactivates the E2 promoter (PMID 1832724), inducing E2F dimerization (PMID 8289811). Literature junction: HAdV-2/HAdV-5 CDS complement(join(..33192,33904..34077)), intron 33193..33903 (PMID 33239457; HAdV-5 numbering from the long-read re-annotation OP218818 of PMID 36095031); verified on AC_000008. No paper gives the junction for other species, so DATABASE-ONLY anchors were also used, each verified on sequence (ATG, GT..AG, clean ORF): HAdV-3 NC_011203, HAdV-12 NC_001460, HAdV-40 NC_001454. Extended to other genomes by pairwise alignment of the donor and acceptor regions to the nearest anchor; where the acceptor region did not align, the unique AG keeping the exon-2 protein in frame; donor rescue likewise. Every distinct product was translated and aligned with the anchors: exon 2 in frame, the conserved C-terminal motif W.[GE]G[GS] present (all four anchors; HAdV-31 reads WEEGS), no ambiguity codes. 2366 of 3199 references rest on a database-only anchor for the donor or acceptor. Mastadenovirus. 616 unique references, products 119-150 aa; min_len = 0.95 x shortest. Replaces the deposit-built references (kept as E4ORF67.fasta.deposit_built), 29/165 of which sat off canonical sites.

E1A_13S.anno: Transcriptional activator and retinoblastoma protein binding E1A, 13S mRNA product (289R in HAdV-5)
E1A_13S.comment: 13S product (proximal 5' splice site); differs from the 12S product only by an internal 46-aa segment (PMID 2968533). Junctions come from the literature: HAdV-5 13S 560..1112,1229.. / 12S 560..974,1229.. (PMID 2958276; verified on AC_000008); HAdV-2 559..1111/973,1226.. (PMID 33239457); HAdV-4 576..1140/1047,1233.. (PMID 2947381, reconstructed from the stated 257/226 aa); BAdV-3 606..1215,1323.. (13S only; the authors' own deposit AF030154, PMID 9918888). Extended to other genomes by aligning the donor and acceptor regions to the nearest anchor (two passes, multiple and pairwise; a genome is kept only where the passes agree); start = the in-frame ATG closest to the protein-aligned start; GT/GC..AG required unless the flanks are conserved in context (>=0.8). The 12S product takes the 13S acceptor (shared exon 2, PMID 15068396) and must reproduce the 13S C-terminus exactly. Every distinct product was translated and aligned with the anchor products: exon 2 must align in frame, the product must end in the E1A exon-2 CtBP motif (PxDLS and variants) or match an anchor's own end (the BAdV-3 211R form lacks it), and products with ambiguity codes were removed. References built from deposits were NOT used: 16/26 HAdV-C 12S deposits gave the right protein with the junction 3 nt early (AG..AA). Mastadenovirus: anchors HAdV-2/4/5 cover species C and E directly; other species and animal lineages are site-alignment extensions, each checked as above. 785 unique references, products 211-292 aa. min_len = 0.95 x the shortest reference product (at 0.9 a simian adenovirus A1335 genome with no reference of its own was called through a relative at 200/169 aa, exon 2 only 8 residues).

VI_MAT.comment: HAdV-5 pVI residues 34-239: cut after 33 (MSGG^AF) and 239 (IVGL^GV); removes pVIn and the 11-aa protease cofactor pVIc. Cut sites are the HAdV-2/5 adenovirus protease (AVP) sites from the literature, carried to every precursor in the collection by pairwise alignment to the HAdV-5 protein; a site is accepted only where the member carries the AVP consensus (M/I/L/V)XGX^G or (M/I/L/V)XGG^X (PMID 2691633) at the aligned residue or uniquely within 2 residues.
